anchor_text: To thank the Master is to obey Him
caption: Maps each of the three debts of gratitude to its corresponding practice.

anchor_text: The first key is affliction, the middle key is guidance, the last key is piety
caption: Shows the three successive keys that open the houses of the hearts.

section: 3. The Five Conditions and the Covenant
anchor_text: the work culminates in the last of them
caption: Shows how each earlier Book points forward to the next, culminating in the last revelation that confirms and supersedes them all.

anchor_text: first the will, then the command, then the saying
caption: Traces how creation issues from light through the three words — will, command, saying — culminating in the divine utterance Kun fa-yakun.

anchor_text: Three things branching from three things before them
caption: Pairs each derived element with its origin among the three primordial words, with air encompassing all as the unique seventh.

anchor_text: Some of them are imams and speakers — natiqs
caption: Shows the ranked bearers of the religion descending from the prophetic houses through arguments and chiefs down to the summoners.

anchor_text: seven things, branching from seven origins
caption: Maps the seven origins from which the world's structure branches.

anchor_text: their opposites in misery are seven as well
caption: Pairs the seven blessings of the world against their seven counterparts in misery.

anchor_text: this world, and everything in it that I have described to you, has an apparent and an inner
caption: Shows the world's outer body sustained by an inner soul that is God.

section: 6. Outer and Inner, Body and Soul
anchor_text: the hidden egg, which has an outward
caption: Shows the three nested layers of knowledge — outward, inward, and inner of the inner — through the egg parable.

section: 6. Outer and Inner, Body and Soul
anchor_text: the creation of the three houses of worship
caption: Maps each layer of knowledge to its corresponding order of creation and the human type it produces.

section: 6. Outer and Inner, Body and Soul
anchor_text: nothing is known except by a name, an attribute, or a meaning
caption: Shows how name and attribute must join to convey meaning, illustrated by the moon example.

section: 8. Returning Home, and the Father's Reckoning
anchor_text: I have resorted to three considerations
caption: Shows the three considerations the Shaykh names to steady himself at parting.

section: 8. Returning Home, and the Father's Reckoning
anchor_text: I enjoin upon you the fear of God who created you
caption: Shows the three charges the Shaykh lays upon the boy as he sends him into the world.

section: 9. Abu Malik and the Trial of the Old Religion
anchor_text: cannot be free of one of three states
caption: Maps the three possible states Abu Malik says the converts must fall into.
